answer_key.provenance: confirmed from the OOM-on-write errors combined with a memory policy that never evicts, so a full cache stops accepting new entries

title: ingress rejecting file uploads

timeline.event: New document-upload feature ships to users; average upload size ~3MB
Upload endpoint returns errors for larger files while small uploads succeed
Backend upload handler never receives the request; rejection happens at the edge proxy

log_excerpts.excerpt: 2026/03/01 10:18:42 [error] client intended to send too large body: 3145728 bytes, returning 413 Request Entity Too Large
annotations: (no nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size set) -> client_max_body_size defaulting to 1m
INFO 0 requests reached the handler for files > 1MB; access log shows no matching upstream entry

answer_key.ground_truth_root_cause: the ingress proxy body-size limit is smaller than the files users upload, so large requests are rejected before reaching the backend
answer_key.provenance: root-caused to a default 1MB proxy body limit against multi-MB uploads, producing 413s at the edge with no backend involvement

title: analytics-service query timeouts during business hours

timeline.event: A schema migration is started against the reporting database during peak reporting load
Read queries begin queueing; nothing is being deleted, but everything waits
PagerDuty critical: analytics query p99 > 30s; queries pile up behind a single blocked statement

log_excerpts.excerpt: LOG: process 4471 still waiting for AccessExclusiveLock on relation events_fact after 30012.114 ms
STATEMENT: ALTER TABLE events_fact ADD COLUMN campaign_id bigint; -- holds the table, blocks all readers
WARN 100% of SELECTs on events_fact blocked; connections healthy, CPU low, they are simply queued behind the ALTER

answer_key.ground_truth_root_cause: a schema migration took a table-wide exclusive lock during peak traffic, blocking all reads on the reporting table
answer_key.provenance: root-caused to an ALTER holding an AccessExclusiveLock while readers queued behind it; there was no deadlock and resources were idle
